plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control DE + GSEA (n=3/3)
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single raw integer gene-level count matrix (counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 6 samples, gene symbols in the first column) produced by STAR alignment plus featureCounts, with a 6-row metadata.csv giving one condition label per sample: 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples, unpaired, single batch. The research question is purely which genes differ between treated and control, so the plan is a straight count-model differential expression workflow with a functional read-out, not a discovery pipeline.

Because the counts come from STAR/featureCounts rather than a transcript quantifier, they are already gene-level integers: they go into the negative binomial model as they are, with no gene-length correction and no tximport import step (rule R-0064). T1S1 runs the sample-structure QC first — library sizes, blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and a sample-distance heatmap — so that an outlier or a failed separation of treated from control is seen before any test is fitted; with 3 vs 3 a single aberrant sample dominates the fit. T1S2 does the modelling: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside DESeq2, design ~condition with control set explicitly as the reference level so that a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated, Wald test, apeglm shrinkage for reported effect sizes and ranking, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on, and the raw p-value histogram inspected before the adjustment is trusted. T1S2b re-runs the same contrast with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test purely as a robustness check; the intersection of the two significant sets is the high-confidence list and the union is never reported as the result.

T2S1 takes the full ranked list of tested genes — ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic, the stated choice among the disputed ranking metrics, because it is signed and scaled by its own standard error and does not tie at the top the way a signed p-value does — and runs fgsea against the human MSigDB hallmark collection, with GO biological process as the follow-up collection. Reactome C2 is the knowledge service's preferred second collection but is not staged in this environment; GO BP is staged and is the named permitted follow-up, so the step uses it and states the substitution. Ranked GSEA rather than over-representation is also the right call on power grounds: with 3 replicates per group the significant list is likely to be short, and an over-representation test on a list under ~50 genes has no power. T1S3 assembles the report and is where the central caveat lives: 3 vs 3 is low power, benchmarks find count models recover only a minority of true differentially expressed genes at that replicate number and mostly those with large fold changes, so absence from the significant list is not evidence that a gene is unchanged, and the alpha is not to be loosened to compensate.

Minimal pre-filter: at least 10 counts in at least 3 samples
~ condition with explicit reference level control; contrast condition treated vs control
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR with independent filtering, p-value histogram inspected
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test as robustness second method
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, then GO BP
Reproducibility report: MA plot, dispersion plot, effect columns, power statement, method overlap, leading edge genes, sessionInfo

steps.name: Differential expression report
steps.question: What is the reproducible, power-aware summary of the treated-vs-control differential expression and enrichment result for these 6 human liver samples?
steps.description: Assemble a single report from T1S1, T1S2, T1S2b and T2S1. State the method, package versions, the design formula ~condition, the explicit contrast (condition, treated, control), the alpha and BH cutoff, the number of genes tested after filtering, and the number of DE genes. Place the MA plot, the dispersion plot and the p-value histogram before the gene tables. Give the gene table with baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange, stat, pvalue and padj, ranked by the shrunken fold change. Report the DESeq2/edgeR overlap and name the intersection as the high-confidence set. Report the enrichment result with its collection, version, ranking metric, universe and size window, and list the leading-edge genes per significant set. Open with an explicit power statement for 3 replicates per group. Close with a reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, seeds, and the gene set collection version.
steps.context: Final synthesis step. The design is 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples from a single batch, quantified by STAR + featureCounts over 12,000 gene symbols. The report must not overstate: at this replicate number the significant list is a small, high-effect-size subset of what is really changing.
acceptance_criteria: A power statement for n=3 per group appears BEFORE the gene tables, stating the replicate number, that count models recover only a minority of true DE genes at that size, and that absence from the list is not evidence of no change
Method, package versions, design formula, contrast direction, thresholds, number of genes tested and number of DE genes all stated
MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histogram included and each explained
Gene table carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE; ranking and plots use the shrunken value while p-values come from the unshrunken fit
DESeq2 vs edgeR counts and intersection size reported; intersection named as high-confidence, union not presented as the result

Enrichment section names the gene set database and version, the ranking metric (Wald statistic), the universe and the size window, and lists leading-edge genes per significant set with the overlap between leading edges marked
A statement that enrichment results are method-dependent and that enriched sets are hypotheses
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions, seeds and collection versions stored with the results
constraints: Do not loosen or re-tune the significance threshold in the report
Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit
Report the number of genes with NA padj and the cause
State the power limit of a 3-vs-3 design before any gene table
Do not describe an enriched gene set as a mechanism established by these data
caveats: A short DE list at 3 vs 3 is the expected outcome, not a failure of the analysis; say so plainly rather than reaching for a looser cutoff
The single-batch claim comes from the metadata, which carries only sample and condition — there is no covariate to test it against, so unmodelled technical structure cannot be excluded

grounding.reason: Report content follows the returned report-step rules: power statement at n=3 (R-0094), two-method overlap (R-0042), shrunken and unshrunken effects (R-0085), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087), method and threshold reporting (R-0041, R-0051), enrichment method-dependence (R-0055), leading edge (R-0105) and the reproducibility record (R-0086).
